story.what_it_does: KPIT Technologies provides software and engineering services to automakers and other vehicle makers, and is shifting toward selling its own products and solutions. In FY26 it earned revenue of ₹64,549 million, with about 71% of work on fixed-price contracts by Sep-26.
story.plans: Management is pivoting from services to solutions and products, aiming for solutions and products to reach 60% of revenue in 3 years and guiding 30% growth there for FY27. It also targets a medium-term EBITDA margin of 22% to 24% and says margins should improve each quarter.
story.moat: The notes show deep ties with big automakers, including two largest accounts and a plan to raise wallet share with a key client. But those same clients are cutting back, and the notes do not give hard evidence of a lasting edge beyond these relationships and its growing products business.

scenarios.story: The two shrinking large accounts bottom out within a couple of quarters, and growth in off-highway, commercial vehicles and products keeps offsetting passenger car weakness. Margins then rise each quarter and growth returns in the second half of FY27.
signals_to_watch: Decline in the two largest accounts bottoming out over the next couple of quarters
EBITDA margin improving each quarter from 17.8% in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue stays roughly flat in constant currency while products and commercial vehicles grow and passenger car declines. Margins recover slowly and well short of the earlier 20% to 21% range for some time.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency growth staying near flat (0.2% year on year in Q2 FY27)
Products revenue growth (25% year on year in Q2 FY27) and its share of revenue

scenarios.story: European and Japanese automakers keep cutting costs and delaying programs, so the large accounts and Qorix keep weakening. Cash conversion slips and the promised turnaround keeps getting pushed out.
signals_to_watch: Europe revenue falling (down 16.3% year on year in Q2 FY27)
DSO rising (53 days) and net cash falling (₹6.2 billion)
